analysis.investment_thesis: Aegis Logistics is the kind of infrastructure-moat business I can walk up to, touch, and understand — it owns tank farms and LPG terminals that India's energy economy cannot function without, and its operating profits have compounded at 21.9% for nine years while the market prices it at a PEG of ~1.4. India's LPG penetration in rural areas is still in early innings, making this a decade-long volume compounder dressed up as a boring logistics company.
key_strengths: Operating income CAGR of 21.9% over 9 years — the revenue line looks volatile due to commodity prices, but the margin-dollar engine is remarkably consistent
Physical infrastructure moat: shore-based tank farms and LPG terminals take years and hundreds of crores to replicate; regulatory approvals add another layer of protection
Net profit trajectory is clean: INR 511 → 672 → 787 Cr over three years with OCF positive all 5 years, confirming earnings quality
key_risks: Revenue is commodity-price linked (swung from INR 8,627 Cr in 2023 to INR 6,764 Cr in 2025), which obscures the underlying volume story and can spook investors
Finance costs have tripled from INR 88 Cr (2023) to INR 165 Cr (2025) as the company funds a large capacity expansion — interest coverage needs monitoring
ROCE at 13.2% is modest and below the 15%+ I'd want for a capital-intensive infrastructure business
red_flags: Total debt jumped to INR 4,606 Cr (2025) vs INR 1,924 Cr (2023) — the expansion is debt-funded and FCF has been negative in recent years
Free cash flow was -INR 386 Cr in 2025 due to INR 945 Cr capex — needs monitoring to ensure returns on new capacity materialize
analysis.detailed_analysis: Aegis is a stalwart on the cusp of becoming a fast grower. The company's liquid and gas terminal network is a near-irreplaceable piece of India's energy supply chain — oil majors, petrochemical companies, and LPG distributors all depend on Aegis's storage and throughput capacity. The P/E of 32.4 applied against 9-year earnings CAGR of 22.6% gives a PEG of ~1.43, which is acceptable for an infrastructure business with this level of moat durability. Promoter holding at 58.1% provides alignment.
